text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: svc=v2-api namespace=prod - 5xx spike, error rate > 40% over 1m. Paging on-call (sam).

alex: I'm seeing the canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff immediately after the deploy. Not routing traffic yet but health checks failing.

sam: on it. can anyone share what changed in the deploy? commit id?

maria: pushed v2-api@9f2c3de about 3 minutes ago. main change was HPA + updated resource requests.

jun: i'm pulling logs now. also +1 to check HPA YAML, we had a flaky template last week.

alex: logs from one canary pod: 
```
Error: failed to start: configmap "v2-config" not found
panic: missing required config
```

linda: that configmap was supposed to be created by the release job, I see it in the job log but name is v2-config-rc not v2-config (templating bug).

sam: ok that explains crashloops. but why is overall service showing 5xx? canary shouldn't route traffic.

maria: we enabled canary traffic at 10% for the rollout automatically via cd pipeline. looks like feature flag gating didn't stick, ff:rollout_v2 = true.

alex: so two problems: bad configmap name + feature flag routed traffic to failing canary.

deploy-bot: deploy v2-api@9f2c3de started 3m ago. canary traffic configured: 10%. HPA applied: hpa-v2-api (minReplicas: "0", maxReplicas: "50", targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 10).

jun: the HPA minReplicas="0" is suspicious — our service had a short window with 0 pods and the external LB marked backends unhealthy, causing 5xx for requests that didn't hit other zones. Also targetCPU 10% will aggressively scale.

sam: immediate mitigation: 1) flip ff:rollout_v2 -> false to stop sending new traffic to canary. 2) create/update configmap with correct name. 3) set HPA minReplicas=2 and remove weird CPU target. 4) rollback if needed.

alex: i can flip the flag via the admin console now. doing it.

alex: done — ff:rollout_v2 -> OFF :white_check_mark:

maria: i'll patch the configmap now with the expected name so pods start. running: 
```
kubectl apply -n prod -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: v2-config
data:
  config.yaml: |
    feature: default
EOF
```

jun: patching HPA: 
```
kubectl patch hpa hpa-v2-api -n prod --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2,"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":60}}'
```

linda: i'm watching pod events. new pods are scheduling, readiness probes passing.

alex: i'm seeing 200s start to return across the board, error rate dropping. dashboard back to baseline in eu-prod.

sam: good. keep the ff off. we need a rollback as a precaution? maria, can you rollback the rollout or do we prefer to patch?

maria: since we already patched config and HPA and traffic is healthy, i'd prefer to pause the rollout and run a validation job. but if anything flaps again we should rollback.

jun: marking this as a RELEASE incident: primary cause = bad manifest templating (configmap name) + aggressive HPA template + feature flag routing enabled by pipeline.

sam: i'm switching incident ownership to on-call changeover in 10m to linda. Linda please take post-mitigation monitoring and postmortem writeup.

linda: acknowledged, will take over and start an incident doc. I'll collect timelines and the release job logs.

deploy-bot: killed canary traffic rule for v2-api in LB.

alex: quick note: build pipeline needs guard to prevent HPA minReplicas 0 and to validate configmap names before promoting.

maria: creating a ticket now: RB-4872 - release safety checks: validate configmap names, prohibit minReplicas<1, require staged ff toggle approval.

sam: thanks everyone. leave monitoring on for 30m, then we'll close. add customer impact notes: ~5% of requests experienced 5xx for ~4 minutes in eu region, no data loss, no auth or billing effects.

linda: adding to incident doc: affected tenants: multiple hosted customers in eu-prod; impact: increased 5xx and latency spike; mitigation: ff disabled, configmap applied, HPA patched.

jun: postmortem owner: linda, timeline + remediation due EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=SEV2 -> status=mitigated by team.

sam: closing handoff: linda you own the follow ups. I'll update on-call rotation notes.

linda: got it. i'll post the postmortem link here when ready. :memo:
